name: Klik / RSI Helper
description: A localhost communication bridge connecting desktop automation with browser-side userscripts.
example: PowerShell and a local HTTP service coordinate with Tampermonkey. The complete automated cycle remains an integration milestone.

name: Entra OAuth Handoff
description: Coordinates interactive Microsoft authentication between PowerShell, the browser, and Microsoft Entra.
example: PowerShell starts the authentication flow, the browser handles interactive sign-in, and the authorized session returns to PowerShell.

name: MuseumOS Bridge
description: Uses the custom mosbridge:// URI protocol to hand browser requests to local Windows automation.
example: A registered URI launches the local protocol handler, which passes the request to PowerShell and the localhost workflow.

name: TM Catapult
description: Connects browser-side JavaScript automation to PowerShell through a localhost HTTP service.
example: A userscript sends a structured request to the local Catapult endpoint on port 8770 for desktop-side processing.

name: Tauri Native Bridge
description: Connects web-based application interfaces to native Rust commands and operating-system functionality.
example: Applications such as Jukebox and Vox Box use the Tauri architecture to bridge frontend interactions with native capabilities.

name: Qt WebChannel
description: Powers communication between Widget Wall's React interface and its Python/PySide6 backend.
example: React invokes an exposed Qt WebChannel method, and Python launches or manages a native desktop widget.
